chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, for Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, there is a rooster. Its feet are in the seventh earth, and its neck is fixed beneath the Throne, and its wings are in the atmosphere. When it is the middle of the night, or the second third from the end of the night, it flaps its wings and crows: 'Subbuh, Quddus, our Lord is Allah, the True Manifest King. So there is no god other than Him, the Lord of the Angels and the Spirit.' Thus the rooster flaps its wings and crows.

key_terms.الرُّوحِ: The Spirit (often referring to Angel Jibril or the divine spirit)
key_terms.سُبُّوحٌ: Glorious (one of the names of Allah)
key_terms.قُدُّوسٌ: Holy (one of the names of Allah)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the cosmic rooster in Shia eschatology and night worship?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi describes a cosmic rooster (Dajaj) whose physical form spans the cosmos, with feet in the seventh earth and neck beneath the Throne, serving as a celestial herald. At the last third of the night, it proclaims the glorification of Allah, echoing the divine attributes mentioned in the Quran, thereby linking the natural order to the spiritual reality of the unseen world. This imagery underscores the Shia belief in the interconnectedness of the physical and metaphysical realms, where creation actively participates in praising its Creator.
